answer: Reputation here is a signed score in a public vault that decays without fresh verifiable work, like pigment fading on unprotected paint. Cloned or dormant identities inherit only that fading score, so fakes gain nothing durable, and every new inlet starts near zero, earning trust only through real, attested tasks. Each sybil therefore costs an attacker the same compute, time, and task fees as one honest agent, and mass duplication buys no shortcut. Cloning to outnumber genuine workers costs more than it returns.
